HypothesizedGapReason: Likely a feature-complete tool in maintenance mode run by one maintainer. After the C-to-Go rewrite and 4.0.0 version prep (Nov 2022) and a HEAD-request tweak (Nov 2023), no commit message points to unfinished work.
WhyRecovered: A Dependabot PR bumping go-chi/chi (2025-06-20) was followed days later by the maintainer bumping Go to 1.23 and updating dependencies.
Notes: Telize was rewritten in Go, then went quiet for 17 months after a small HEAD-request feature. Activity resumed with a Dependabot bump and a routine dependency refresh by the same maintainer, so the gap looks like maintenance mode rather than abandonment. Only 3 commits follow the gap in the WoC data, and GitHub shows a later commit (2026/07/09).

HypothesizedGapReason: Single-developer research code. Pre-gap commits include merges from the Auto-LV-Modeling repo and vague messages ("Updates", "Path changes"), which suggests work had moved to that other repo.
WhyRecovered: May 2024 commits add optional scaling, a natural-sort bug fix, mesh-motion improvements and cubic-spline interpolation, i.e. new simulation features for the same pipeline.
Notes: The 26-month gap follows a stretch where the lone developer was merging from another repo (Auto-LV-Modeling) with terse messages. The same developer came back in May 2024 with feature and bug-fix work, then slowed again; GitHub shows the last commit on 2025/02/28, so it is marked Inactive. The cause is inferred, not stated in any commit.

ASPECT has no gap of 3 or more months: it has 23,494 commits from 347 authors and roughly 1,600-2,200 commits every year since 2014. Recent history is mostly PR merges and CI runner fixes, which shows an actively maintained community project.

HypothesizedGapReason: The original research authors (Bergstra, Komer, Warde-Farley) were active in 2014 and went quiet after the regression support commit (Oct 2014). The commit messages do not state a reason.
WhyRecovered: In May 2016 Komer merged upstream and updated the SVM gamma parameter for new scikit-learn syntax, then Li Shen added regression and time-series lag selectors and Chandler Watson ran 2to3 for Python 3.
WhoRecovered: Mixed: original author Brent Komer restarted it, but new contributors (Li Shen, Chandler Watson) did most of the work
Notes: After early work by the research authors in 2014, the project sat idle for 18 months. It revived in 2016 when scikit-learn API changes and new contributors (regression and Python 3 support) pulled it back. A 2025 burst by a new maintainer (sklearn 1.5/1.6 support, new PyPI version) ended on 2025/03/22, just before the cutoff, so it is marked Inactive.

HypothesizedGapReason: Looks like a short pause after the repo was scaffolded (first commit, README, FastQC prototype, Slack link fix, all in late July 2019). The 4-month gap is the shortest of the set.
WhyRecovered: The Dec 2019 commits add GitHub Actions CI plus the first real module files (FastQC, samtools sort/index, TrimGalore), so the repo moved from scaffold to working modules.
WhoRecovered: Same core team (Phil Ewels, who also appears before the gap, and Harshil Patel/drpatelh)
Notes: This is a fork (1 star, 0 forks) of the nf-core modules repo, so its history is really the upstream project. The only gap of 3+ months is a 4-month pause after the July 2019 scaffolding, ended by CI setup and the first modules from the same core team. Activity then grew steadily to 8,188 commits and 619 authors.

HypothesizedGapReason: The pre-gap commits are a burst of merging "Jeff's changes" and fixing CUDA and LAPACK build errors by one developer, and activity then stops after Nov 2024. The messages give no explicit reason.
WhyRecovered: Two pull requests (#23, #24) on 2025-10-21 corrected input files for c2h4 and c2h4p (fixed carbon masses).
WhoRecovered: A new contributor (Angela, via PRs) merged by the existing maintainer Adam Hogan
Notes: A small research-code project where one developer pushed build and CUDA fixes in a burst, then went quiet for 10 months. The restart is only 4 commits on a single day, from a new contributor fixing input data, so recovery is weak. GitHub shows 2025/10/21 as the last commit, which keeps it Active under the 2025-09-30 rule.

WebAPI has no gap of 3 or more months across 7,861 commits and 211 authors. Activity peaked in 2018-2019 (about 1,500-1,700 commits a year), fell to 252 in 2023, rebounded to 622 in 2024, and recent history is dominated by Dependabot updates with occasional features (Snowflake key-pair authentication).

HypothesizedGapReason: The 10 commits before the gap are all auto-generated "Merge <sha> into <sha>" pull-request refs from a single day (2021-10-12) and say nothing about the project. The real cause is not visible in commit messages.
WhyRecovered: A Travis-to-GitHub-Actions migration with tests against multiple Postgres/PostGIS versions (Aug 2022), then test updates and protobuf dependency updates.
WhoRecovered: Mixed: François de Metz (earlier PR contributor) and an outside contributor (dflo) restarted it, and the original maintainer Oliver Tonnhofer returned within weeks
Notes: The commits before the gap are synthetic PR-merge refs, so the commit messages cannot explain the 8-month pause. It recovered in mid-2022 through a CI migration (Travis to GitHub Actions) and test fixes, with maintainer Oliver Tonnhofer back on board, and was active with real fixes (tilelist deadlock, PostGIS cleanup) in Sept 2025. The cause needs a check of GitHub issues and PRs from late 2021.

HypothesizedGapReason: A single-author analysis repo whose last pre-gap commit is "add preprint link" (2023-07-11), which suggests the analysis was finished and published as a preprint.
WhyRecovered: N/A. The single follow-up commit (2024-11-26) reorders cohorts to match the manuscript, probably tied to a manuscript revision.
Notes: This analysis repo went quiet after the preprint link was added in July 2023, which fits a finished project. One later commit aligns cohort order with the manuscript, probably a revision, and nothing has followed (GitHub last commit 2024/11/26), so it is Inactive. It has only one author in practice (6 listed), so the pattern is easy to read as a study lifecycle.

HypothesizedGapReason: The maintainer wrote in the March 2017 commit that the Julia 0.6 syntax update is not backward compatible with 0.5, so he avoided merging it, and the julia06 branch waited until Jan 2018. This is the clearest gap explanation in the set.
WhyRecovered: "Merge branch 'julia06'" on 2018-01-17, followed by new features (FITS header keywords, map plotting) and a split of the code into smaller files.
Notes: The gap is explained by the maintainer's own commit message: Julia 0.6 changes were held back because they broke 0.5 compatibility, and were merged in Jan 2018. After the gap the same maintainer added features, and later history is mostly Dependabot, version bumps and docs, so the project is Active.
